summary: GearboxAI: Dedicated pool autoscale + model fallback loop causing elevated 5xxs and streaming disconnects
description:
Issue summary: On 2026-03-12 13:02 UTC GearboxAI reported application-side timeouts and streaming disconnects while using their Reserved Dedicated pool. Symptoms included repeated 5xxs from our API, automatic model fallback between gptx-7b-redwood-v1 and a quantized fallback variant (gptx-7b-q4b), and a billing spike from repeated retry loops. Impact: customer-facing API failures for GearboxAI's production traffic (~120 RPS) and degraded QA sessions for their internal users. Total outage window for the most severe errors: ~34 minutes.

Timeline (high level):
- 2026-03-12 12:58 UTC: first alert from internal monitoring (elevated 5xx rate in us-west dedicated pool).
- 2026-03-12 13:02 UTC: GearboxAI escalates via support channel (severity P0 request).
- 2026-03-12 13:07 UTC: Support triage; SRE engaged and created INC-2026-0317.
- 2026-03-12 13:12 UTC: Observed autoscaler triggering double-scaling events and several node reconnects.
- 2026-03-12 13:20 UTC: Serving runtime started to route traffic to fallback quantized model due to transient OOM errors; fallback routing created retry loops for some requests.
- 2026-03-12 13:36 UTC: Mitigation applied: temporarily pinned GearboxAI routing to stable model on separate pool and disabled aggressive autoscale policy.
- 2026-03-12 13:50 UTC: 5xx rate subsided and streaming reconnect rate returned to baseline.

Steps to reproduce (internal):
1) Use traffic generator with incremental RPS up to 150 against dedicated pool in us-west with model pinning unset.
2) Simulate instance pre-emption by restarting GPU worker while autoscaler configured with burst_policy=aggressive.
3) Observe serving-runtime logs for repeated fallback_to_quantized and request_requeue messages.

Logs/snippets: (excerpts pasted into ticket comments and log archive)
- serving-runtime: "ERROR request_handler - failed to allocate KV cache: OOM on GPU0 -> falling back to gptx-7b-q4b"
- scheduler: "WARN autoscaler - scale_up triggered twice in 15s for pool=gearbox-enterprise-pool"
comments: Lina Ortiz (2026-03-12T13:05:00Z): Customer reports intermittent streaming disconnects and HTTP 500 spikes. Customer reports that their application saw ~30% error rate at peak. Initial ask: urgent investigation and ETA for recovery.

Mikhail Petrov (2026-03-12T13:10:00Z): Triage: SRE to confirm whether autoscaler or serving runtime is root cause. Assigning INT-4120 to infra team to check autoscaler logs. Marking as Sev0 and paging on-call infra/sre.

SRE-OnCall (2026-03-12T13:22:00Z): Observed repeated node reboots during the incident window; autoscaler double-fired after transient GPU agent heartbeat delay. Investigating heartbeat jitter causing duplicate scale events. See Slack thread #inc-2026-0317: https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C02INC/12345

Eng-Serving (2026-03-12T13:28:00Z): Serving runtime shows OOM transitions on hot KV cache for gptx-7b-redwood-v1 leading to immediate fallback to q4 variant. Fallback triggers client retries which loop due to routing policy not tagging reduced-capacity variants as 'no-retry'. Patch candidate ready: infra PR https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/784

Customer (GearboxAI - Alex Chen) (2026-03-12T13:30:00Z): Thanks for the rapid response. Please advise if we should throttle traffic or pin to a specific model while you investigate. We are seeing billing spikes due to retries; this is impacting customer SLAs.

Mikhail Petrov (2026-03-12T13:36:00Z): Temporary mitigation applied: pinned GearboxAI to gptx-7b-redwood-v1 on a reserve node group and disabled aggressive autoscaler burst policy for that pool. Monitoring metrics now.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: Autoscaler double-scale due to heartbeat jitter caused brief worker churn -> worker reconnects triggered serving-runtime failover and fallback routing.

Hypothesis B: KV cache memory pressure (growth spike) caused OOM on some GPU workers for the non-quantized model; runtime fallback to quantized variant combined with client retry policy produced looping 5xxs.

Logs indicate both firing: autoscaler fired duplicate scale_up events (infra logs) and serving-runtime reported multiple OOM events within the same 90s window. CPU/memory metrics around 13:10-13:25 show KV cache growth correlated with request bursts. See monitoring dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/gearbox/dedicated-pool-oom

Reproduction on staging: reproduced using synthetic RPS with config burst_policy=aggressive + worker restart; fallback loop observed consistently. Fix candidate: mark fallback variants as non-retryable OR add short throttling cooldown on fallback events.

Root cause (post-analysis): combination of autoscaler heartbeat jitter + KV cache mis-sizing for observed request distribution. Autoscaler duplicate scale caused temporary overcommit and reconnect churn; during reconnect the runtime's KV cache allocation failed and triggered immediate fallback routing. Retry policy coupled with fallback produced request storms and billing leak.
Related PRs: https://github.com/redwood/serving-runtime/pull/829 (add non-retry flag for fallback variants), https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/784 (debounce autoscaler triggers)
Related internal ticket: INT-4120 (autoscaler debounce investigation).
resolution_summary: Mitigations applied during incident: (1) temporarily pinned GearboxAI to stable model on reserve node group, (2) disabled aggressive autoscaler burst policy for their pool, (3) emergency patch to mark fallback variants non-retry applied to serving-runtime and rolled to prod (PR #829). Long-term fixes scheduled: autoscaler debounce (PR #784) and KV cache sizing adjustment for enterprise pools. Customer confirmed recovery and error rate returned to baseline by 13:50 UTC.
post_incident_actions: Engineering: Merge and deploy autoscaler debounce PR (#784) across prod clusters by 2026-03-18.
Serving Runtime: Adjust default KV cache sizing heuristics for reserved pools and add proactive telemetry for KV growth by 2026-03-19.
SDK/Client: Update retry policy defaults to avoid retrying immediately after a fallback route; publish advisory for enterprise customers by 2026-03-20.
Customer Success: Scheduled 1:1 with GearboxAI on 2026-03-15 to review incident, share postmortem and discuss credits/compensation.
Billing: Investigate invoice exposure and prepare credit proposal for retry-driven overages; due 2026-03-16.
billing_impact_notes: GearboxAI reported an estimated 12% overage on their daily usage during the incident window due to retry loops. Billing team to quantify token-level overcharge and propose credit. Temporary mitigation to prevent further charge accrual was applied by pinning routing and disabling retries on fallback variants.
customer_communication_summary: Initial notification sent via support at 13:05 UTC. Real-time updates provided in support channel and Slack incident thread. After recovery, emailed customer a summary and next steps at 14:10 UTC. Follow-up 1:1 scheduled for 2026-03-15. Customer acknowledged and accepted the mitigation path; asked for formal postmortem and credit proposal.
resolution_notes: Incident closed after targeted mitigations and two hotfixes deployed. Monitoring alert thresholds adjusted to detect duplicate scale events earlier. No further customer-impacting recurrences observed in 72h window.
